column1: # EXP-R2-244 stage 29: three further protein arms on the frozen MegaScale
# designed referent, at each arm's own declared rendering.
# THE ESTIMAND IS UNCHANGED AND NOTHING ABOUT IT IS REDRAWN. Per wild type, the
# Spearman correlation between an arm's summed log-likelihood of a rendered
# variant and that variant's measured folding stability, ddG_ML, which is the
# column ProteinGym itself publishes as DMS_score for its 64 Tsuboyama assays.
# Per-wild-type correlations are averaged inside a unit and the unit is
# resampled; a design's unit is its design series and a natural's is WT_cluster.
# The cohort is the census certified by EXP-R2-190 and not a draw: 412 wild types
# and 527,204 variants in all, of which 130 certified zero-hit design wild types
# over 40 series (36 of them wholly zero-hit) carry 110,730 variants and 266
# natural domains over 124 WT_cluster units carry 404,114. The MIN_VARIANTS = 30
# floor is already applied, so the smallest wild type carries 488 variants; the
# scored set is every wild type, and the design side of the analysis is the 130
# certified zero-hit ones. The cohort artefact is the file whose SHA-256 is
# staged once at the run root and read by every cell through --cohort; each
# payload recomputes that digest and stage_analyse refuses a mismatch. The
# baselines and the free and fragment-level gates are the frozen ones
# (results/transfer/designed_referent/baselines.json); no baseline is recomputed
# and no threshold is retuned. The verdict rule is designed_referent.arm_verdict
# and is applied afterwards, not here.
# WHY THE RUN EXISTS. Stage 29's door admitted a panel member or a staged scale
# rung, so the three checkpoints below were unreachable however well their corpus
# identification was recorded. It now admits the union of the declared protein
# doors -- the panel, EXP-R2-224's scale rungs, EXP-R2-225's second-stage
# checkpoints and the budget-only candidate checkpoints -- each listed one by
# one, and still narrower than "any arm": a text arm in the same tuple is refused
# by its own modality, a joint checkpoint reached by path is in no door, and the
# ProGen3 rungs stay behind EXCLUDED_ARMS. Reaching an arm is not scoring it, so
# this campaign scores it.
# WHAT EACH SCORER ACTUALLY RENDERS, read from each arm's own declaration rather
# than assumed. rita-xl declares eos_bounded_seq and is scored by
# rita_fitness.RitaFitnessScorer: the document boundary <EOS>, then the sequence,
# with the tokenizer's terminal <EOS> still appended, and both marker positions
# excluded from the scored targets because they carry one id, so the scored
# targets are the sequence's residues. That scorer assigns no pad token and takes
# no attention mask, so it refuses a variable-length batch and pads nothing; all
# variants of one wild type have one length, so every batch is an equal-length
# substitution batch and the refusal never fires. proteinglm-7b-clm declares
# gmask_sop_eos and is scored on the served continuation: the native
# <gmask><sop><eos> prefix and then residues 2..L, with the prefix and residue 1
# not scored. That is a different scoring functional from a full-protein
# left-to-right sum and is labelled as one in the payload rather than described
# as one. protgpt3-1.3b declares bos_direction_seq and renders <|bos|> then the
# N-to-C direction token then the sequence; both markers are prefix ids and one of
# them, the direction token, sat inside the old all-valid sum, so the scorer now
# resolves the scored span from target_rule(input_format) together with
# rendering_marker_ids(arm) and the direction token is context rather than
# content. Measured on the tiny cohort on Compute before dispatch: a 40-residue
# sequence scores 41 positions under the old all-valid rule and 40 under the new
# one, one column per record at the direction token's position, and the markers
# this arm's rendering declares are ids 1 and 4.
# PRECISION IS A PROPERTY OF THE CHECKPOINT, NOT A SPEED KNOB. rita-xl and
# proteinglm-7b-clm are float32: rita_fitness refuses any other inference
# precision, and ProteinGLM's derived serving package refuses one too. At float32
# a TF32 matmul is a different arithmetic rather than a faster one, so the stage
# checks the live policy against precision_policy's single declaration and refuses
# a mismatch, and the three observed policy fields travel in the payload. TF32 is
# NOT enabled to shorten this run. protgpt3-1.3b is scored at the panel's
# bfloat16. One precision per arm, and the precision each payload was taken at is
# in its own settings block.
# THE SCORING STRATUM IS RECORDED, AND THE SIX PAYLOADS THAT PREDATE THE FIELD
# ARE LEFT ALONE. All three payloads carry scoring_stratum
# n_to_c_summed_log_likelihood, as the three EXP-R2-226 rungs already did; the
# six panel payloads written on 2026-08-13 and 2026-08-25 record none, and they
# are neither re-scored here nor edited here. Adding the field to them by hand
# would synthesise a label no run recorded, which is the thing
# scale_comparison.require_uniform_stratum refuses a payload for, so that refusal
# is left standing rather than edited away. A payload that records a stratum
# outside the three declared ones is refused at analysis.
# PROGEN3 IS NOT IN THIS CAMPAIGN AND ITS EXCLUSION IS UNCHANGED. Both rungs'
# published scoring convention is the mean of the N-to-C and C-to-N summed
# log-likelihoods, which is a different stratum from the left-to-right sum every
# arm here is read under, and this stage has no bidirectional door: stage 29
# scores by summing left-to-right next-token log-likelihoods and reaches an arm
# through arms.arm_spec. The record already states what a ProGen3 MegaScale row
# would require -- a route needing no ArmSpec together with the lineage's own
# bidirectional scorer, a per-rung ARM_IDENTIFICATION entry, and stratum
# labelling -- and opening that route also narrows a refusal that
# 43_second_stage_capability.py reads and three guard tests pin. That is a
# separate capability and it is not half-built here.
# CARDS. cuda:0 and cuda:3 only, which were the two cards idle on this
# allocation when the campaign was written; cuda:1 and cuda:2 carried another
# agent's running cells and are not named here. An earlier revision of this file
# named cuda:2 and cuda:3, and cuda:2 acquired a 4,342 MiB cell between that
# check and this one -- which is why the cards are re-read in the pod immediately
# before dispatch rather than taken from the check before it. The queue runner
# refuses a card that is not idle rather than sharing it, so a card that goes busy
# after this line is written fails a cell loudly instead of corrupting two
# measurements, and a refused cell is not complete and is re-dispatched rather
# than counted. Slot 1 holds the two expensive cells; slot 2 holds the cheapest.
